 Salt Lake City, Utah (KUTV) — Two products recalled by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission on November 12 could pose injury risks. Consumers should stop using the affected products and contact the companies for remedies.
 Huffy is recalling about 286 Buzz Bicycles Cerana T2 pedal-assist e-trikes, model E4004. The rear wheels can loosen or separate from the frame, creating a fall hazard. Huffy has received 12 reports of wheels loosening or separating, resulting in three injuries, including sprains, bruises and abrasions.
 The trikes were sold at independent bike shops nationwide and online from November 2024 through July 2026 for $1,400 to $2,500. Owners should stop using them and contact Huffy for free replacement rear axle assemblies. Huffy will reimburse up to $100 for third-party repair costs.

 Cummins is recalling about 2,960 Onan P5000iDF EFI dual-fuel portable generators. Incorrectly installed valves can prevent fuel vapors from venting properly, allowing pressure to build in the gasoline tank. 
 Fuel may discharge or the cap may eject, posing fire and burn hazards. The company has received 11 reports, including one report of a consumer being splashed with fuel; no medical care was required.
 The dark gray generators were sold at Camping World, Factory Pure, Northern Tool and AP Electric stores, and online at Cummins.com from May 2025 through August 2026 for $1,640 to $1,930. 
 Owners should stop using them, check the model and part number on Cummins’ recall page, and contact an authorized service location to arrange a free repair.
